newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle slow at $66, off $1 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle slow at $66, off $1 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were slow, with light sales noted at $66.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from Friday, feedlot sources and USDA said.

About 600 head sold in Kansas at $66.00, but sources said there were not enough slaughter steers or heifers sold for a market test. There were 5,800 head for the week to date including late Friday and over the weekend, USDA said.

There were no sales early in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, but late sales could develop if some feedyards feel compelled to sell following the decline in Kansas fed cattle prices, they said.
There were 9,300 head confirmed for the week to date near midday for the Panhandle.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by steep declines last week for beef prices and continued beef weakness at midday.

Prices also were weakened by projections for increased cattle supplies in the coming weeks. The Panhandle showlist this week was estimated near 64,000 head, up about 3,000 and the Kansas showlist was pegged near 79,000, up 3,000.
